title: Request-slice causal attributor for per-token latency & cache impact
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Goal: build a low-overhead, causally-grounded attribution system that maps per-request per-token emission timing and KV cache effects to cost/latency metrics. Deliverables: (1) runtime tracing hooks that annotate token emission slices with causal IDs and cache hit/miss markers; (2) probabilistic sampling instrumentation to limit overhead; (3) enrichment processors in the metrics/log pipeline to correlate spans and compute token-level attribution aggregates; (4) Grafana dashboards and alerting rules for token-based latency regressions and cache degradation.

Background: Current tracing provides request- and model-level spans but lacks stable linkage between token emission events and backend kernel/cache events. The result is noisy cost allocation and inability to quantify cache hit impact on per-token latency. This ticket aims to create a lightweight causal attributor that works with existing tracing (OTel) and our batching runtime.

Approach:
- Insert a short-lived 'slice_id' on each emission slice boundary in the serving runtime (C++/Rust runtime hooks). The slice_id is propagated to downstream kernel/launch spans and to the KV cache hit/miss events.
- Implement probabilistic sampling: full payload traces at 0.5% of requests; slice-level micro-traces for sampled requests; aggregated counters for non-sampled requests. Sampling rate configurable per-route via runtime flags.
- Add a compact token-metadata envelope emitted to logs (ndjson) only for sampled slices: {slice_id, token_offset, model_variant, kv_hit, micro_latency_ms}. For non-sampled requests we emit summarized counters per-request.
- Enrich logs/spans in the pipeline (Fluentd -> Kafka -> enrichment service) to join slice_ids and compute causal attributions: per-token attributable kernel time, cache delta contribution, and per-model cost allocation. Use a sliding-window join to bound memory.
- Backfill and calibration: run synthetic workloads to calibrate sampling biases and produce correction coefficients for aggregated estimates.

Trade-offs and constraints:
- Instrumentation must not add >0.5% p99 latency. Probabilistic sampling reduces overhead but needs corrective modeling to estimate population-level cost.
- Propagating slice_id requires minor ABI changes in runtime; we'll gate via feature flag for Dedicated & Hosted initially.
- The enrichment service introduces eventual consistency; dashboards will surface both sampled raw traces and stitched aggregated estimates with confidence intervals.

Acceptance criteria:
- Trace propagation implemented and feature-flagged in runtime; unit tests and e2e smoke tests.
- Enrichment job processing slice_ids at production throughput (tested on staging with 2M requests/day equivalent).
- Grafana dashboards showing per-token median/p95 latency, cache-hit delta attribution, and a reliability panel for sampling confidence.
- Documentation (Confluence) for SDK/trace semantics and for how to interpret inferred estimates.
